places.summary_en: A peaceful lake at the heart of Hanoi, where everyday life meets the legend of the returned sword.
places.history_en: The name means Lake of the Returned Sword. A well-known legend tells how Emperor Lê Lợi returned a magical sword to a golden turtle here after his victory over Ming forces. This story is a legend rather than a documented historical event.
places.culture_en: The lake is a gathering place for walks, morning exercise and conversations. Turtle Tower stands on a small island. Ngọc Sơn Temple and the red Húc Bridge are nearby. This marker shows the lake, not a temple entrance.
places.address: Hoàn Kiếm Lake, Hoàn Kiếm, Hà Nội
places.opening_hours: Open 24 hours. Ngọc Sơn Temple: Tuesday–Sunday 08:00–18:00.
places.booking_info: No booking required for the lake promenade (always free). Ngoc Son Temple on the island charges 30,000 VND, payable at the gate.
places.best_time_to_visit: Early morning (06:00–08:00) for locals' exercise routines, or dusk (17:30–19:00) for the lit-up bridge. Weekends are livelier but more crowded.

places.summary_en: Quiet courtyards, ancient stone stelae and a lasting celebration of learning.
places.history_en: Văn Miếu was established in 1070 under Emperor Lý Thánh Tông. Quốc Tử Giám, the imperial academy, followed in 1076. The complex preserves a long tradition of education and respect for scholars.
places.culture_en: Courtyards and turtle-mounted doctoral stelae reflect the importance of study in Vietnamese culture. Dress respectfully and avoid touching the stone monuments. The marker indicates the heritage complex.
places.booking_info: Tickets sold at the main gate (58 Quoc Tu Giam). No advance booking required for individuals. Group bookings (10+ people) can be arranged through the heritage centre office.
places.best_time_to_visit: Weekday mornings (08:00–10:00) are quietest. Avoid Sunday afternoons during school holidays. Mid-morning light is best for photographs.

places.name_vi: Lăng Chủ tịch Hồ Chí Minh
places.summary_en: The mausoleum where President Ho Chi Minh's body is preserved, at the heart of Ba Dinh Square.
places.history_en: Ho Chi Minh, the founding father of modern Vietnam, died on 2 September 1969. His mausoleum was built on Ba Dinh Square, where he read the Declaration of Independence in 1945. The building, opened in 1975, draws millions of visitors each year. Ho Chi Minh requested a simple cremation, but the government chose to preserve his body in a glass sarcophagus.
places.culture_en: Dress conservatively (no shorts, covered shoulders). Silence and respectful behaviour are required inside. Photography is not permitted in the main hall. Bags and cameras must be left at the cloakroom. The queue can be long; arrive early.
places.address: 2 Hùng Vương, Ba Đình, Hà Nội
places.opening_hours: Tue–Thu and Sat–Sun 07:30–10:30. Closed Monday and Friday. Also closed Sep–Nov for annual maintenance.
places.booking_info: No booking required. Free entry. Arrive by 08:00 to avoid long queues. Leave bags at the cloakroom (free of charge).
places.best_time_to_visit: Arrive before 08:00 for shortest queues. Avoid public holidays when queues are very long.

places.summary_en: A dense and lively labyrinth of 36 streets, each historically named for the trade it once housed.
places.history_en: Hanoi's Old Quarter dates to the 11th century. Each street was traditionally associated with a craft or trade: Hàng Bạc for silver, Hàng Đào for silk, Hàng Mã for paper offerings. The area became a commercial centre under the Lý Dynasty and retains its historic character despite modernisation.
places.culture_en: Bargaining is accepted in many small shops. Watch for motorbikes on narrow pavements. Street food vendors are authentic and affordable. The weekend night market (Fri–Sun 19:00–23:00) brings a festive atmosphere. Respect local residents' space.
places.address: Phố cổ, Hoàn Kiếm, Hà Nội
places.booking_info: No booking required. Free access to all streets. Some individual attractions inside the quarter may charge separately.
places.best_time_to_visit: Evenings for atmosphere and street food. Weekend nights for the pedestrian market. Early mornings reveal a quieter, more local side.

places.summary_en: A former French colonial prison known as the 'Hanoi Hilton', now a museum of Vietnamese history and resilience.
places.history_en: Built by French colonial authorities in 1896 to hold Vietnamese political prisoners, Hoa Lo Prison became a symbol of resistance. After 1954 it held American prisoners of war, who nicknamed it the 'Hanoi Hilton'. Part of the site was demolished to build Hanoi Towers; the surviving section is now a museum.
places.culture_en: Exhibitions present history from the Vietnamese perspective. The tone is serious and reflective. Allow at least an hour to read the exhibits thoughtfully. Photography is permitted in most areas. Dress appropriately.
places.address: 1 Hoả Lò, Hoàn Kiếm, Hà Nội
places.booking_info: Tickets sold at the entrance gate. No advance booking required.
places.best_time_to_visit: Weekday mornings are least crowded. Allow at least one hour to read the exhibits.

foods_restaurants.description_en: Rice noodles in fragrant beef broth, with slices of beef and fresh herbs. A classic Hanoi breakfast, also enjoyed at other times of day.
foods_restaurants.address: 49 Bát Đàn, Hoàn Kiếm, Hà Nội

foods_restaurants.description_en: Charcoal-grilled pork served with rice vermicelli, herbs and a sweet-savoury dipping broth. A favourite Hanoi lunchtime meal.
foods_restaurants.address: 1 Hàng Mành, Hoàn Kiếm, Hà Nội

foods_restaurants.description_en: Marinated catfish fried in turmeric and galangal, finished tableside in a sizzling pan with fresh dill and spring onions. Served with rice vermicelli, peanuts and shrimp paste. Hà Nội has an entire street named after this dish.
foods_restaurants.address: 14 Chả Cá, Hoàn Kiếm, Hà Nội

foods_restaurants.description_en: A crispy baguette filled with pâté, cold cuts, pickled daikon and carrot, fresh coriander, jalapeño and mayonnaise. The Vietnamese take on a French colonial ingredient, now a beloved street food worldwide.
foods_restaurants.address: 25 Hàng Cá, Hoàn Kiếm, Hà Nội

foods_restaurants.description_en: A Hanoian invention: robusta espresso topped with a thick, creamy meringue of egg yolk and condensed milk. Served hot or iced. Created by Nguyễn Văn Giảng in the 1940s when milk was scarce.
foods_restaurants.address: 39 Nguyễn Hữu Huân, Hoàn Kiếm, Hà Nội

foods_restaurants.description_en: A cold rice vermicelli dish topped with sautéed beef, bean sprouts, pickled vegetables, crushed peanuts, fried shallots and herbs, dressed with a sweet-savoury fish sauce. Lighter than a soup, full of texture.
foods_restaurants.restaurant_name: Bún Bò Nam Bộ Bát Đàn
foods_restaurants.address: 67 Hàng Điếu, Hoàn Kiếm, Hà Nội

phrases.usage_note_en: A general greeting suitable for any time of day.
A simple expression of thanks. Add 'rất' before 'cảm ơn' (rất cảm ơn) for 'thank you very much'.
Use to apologise or to politely get someone's attention. Example: 'Xin lỗi, nhà vệ sinh ở đâu?' (Excuse me, where is the toilet?)
A general farewell. 'Hẹn gặp lại' (hen gap lie) means 'see you again'.
Point to the item you mean. Example: Point at a souvenir and say 'Cái này bao nhiêu tiền?'
Useful at markets. Not every price is negotiable. Use politely and smile.
Ask staff for a menu when seated at a restaurant.
Tell the kitchen your preference. 'Ít cay' (ít guy) means 'a little spicy'.
Ask for the bill after your meal. Waving your hand while saying this is understood.
Useful in restaurants or public places. 'Toilet' is also widely understood.

phrases.english_meaning: I would like to go to Hoan Kiem Lake

phrases.usage_note_en: You can also show the written place name to a taxi or xe ôm driver.

events.description_en: Vietnam's most important festival, Tết marks the arrival of the lunar new year. Hanoians return home, decorate with peach blossoms and kumquat trees, visit family and set off fireworks at midnight. The city is simultaneously quieter (many businesses close) and electric (flower markets, festive streets). Hoan Kiem Lake is a focal point for the midnight celebrations.
events.recurrence_note: Annually in January or February — exact date follows the lunar calendar. Public holiday for 7 days. Many shops and restaurants close for 3–10 days around Tết.
events.location_name: Citywide; Hoan Kiem Lake for midnight fireworks

events.description_en: The Mid-Autumn Festival centres on children, lanterns and mooncakes. Families gather on the 15th night of the 8th lunar month. Hàng Mã street in the Old Quarter fills with paper lanterns, lion dance troupes perform, and mooncakes are gifted. The festival predates Vietnamese written history.
events.recurrence_note: Annually on the 15th day of the 8th lunar month (September or October). Not a public holiday, but widely celebrated.
events.location_name: Hàng Mã Street, Old Quarter, Hoàn Kiếm

events.name_vi: Chợ đêm Hàng Ngang – Hàng Đào
events.description_en: Every Friday, Saturday and Sunday evening the streets of Hàng Ngang, Hàng Đào and surrounding lanes transform into a pedestrian market. Local food vendors, handicraft stalls, street performances and crowds of locals and tourists fill the Old Quarter. No cars or motorbikes are allowed in the zone during market hours.
events.recurrence_note: Every Friday, Saturday and Sunday from 19:00 to 23:00.
events.location_name: Hàng Ngang – Hàng Đào, Old Quarter, Hoàn Kiếm

events.description_en: One of Vietnam's longest religious festivals, drawing pilgrims and tourists to the Huong Son mountain complex 60 km south of Hanoi. Visitors travel by rowing boat along the Yen Stream through limestone scenery to reach the pagodas. The highlight is the Huong Tich cave. The journey takes half a day and is an experience in itself.
events.recurrence_note: Opens from the 6th day of the first lunar month through the end of the 3rd lunar month (approximately February to April). Peak visits in the first two weeks.
events.location_name: Huong Son, Mỹ Đức District, Hà Nội (60 km south of city centre)

events.description_en: A national holiday honouring the legendary founders of Vietnam, the Hung Kings. Rituals are held at Nghia Linh mountain in Phu Tho province, 80 km from Hanoi, culminating on the 10th day of the 3rd lunar month. Many Hanoians make the pilgrimage to pay their respects.
events.recurrence_note: 10th day of the 3rd lunar month (typically April). National public holiday.
events.location_name: Đền Hùng, Phú Thọ Province (80 km from Hanoi)

events.name_en: Lim Festival — Quan Họ Folk Singing
events.description_en: The Hội Lim festival celebrates Quan Họ, a traditional form of alternating folk song between male and female singers, now a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. Held on Lim Hill in Bắc Ninh province 30 km from Hanoi, the festival features performers in traditional dress singing from rowing boats on a lake, alongside folk games and ceremonies.
events.recurrence_note: 13th day of the first lunar month (typically February). Easy day trip from Hanoi by bus.
events.location_name: Lim Hill, Tiên Du, Bắc Ninh Province (30 km from Hanoi)
